sections.h2: What does selling a house in McHenry, Illinois involve?
sections.html:
A McHenry owner has three practical paths. You can market the house through an agent, market it on your own, or hand it to a buyer who wants it exactly as it sits and does not need a lender. After the contract is signed, all three paths lead to the same county filing: a transfer declaration plus a recorded deed.

Condition and calendar decide which path fits. A tidy house with time to spare can wait out showings. A house with deferred repairs, a tenant in place, a probate delay or a closing deadline usually points toward the direct sale.

What follows sticks to McHenry itself: Census figures, the permit rules at 333 S Green Street, how city water accounts change hands, and what the county recorder expects.

sections.h2: What kind of city is McHenry, and who is buying here?
sections.html:
McHenry sits on the Fox River in east-central McHenry County. The city's own history page places it 55 miles northwest of the Chicago Loop and 35 miles from O'Hare, centered on Illinois Route 31 and Illinois Route 120, with roughly 13 square miles of land.

Its roots are a river-resort past. By the 1920s the Fox River and nearby lakes had made the town a summer destination, and summer cottages spread along the river. A later wave of subdivisions was annexed from the late 1940s on, so many streets are lined with houses built in the postwar decades.

McHenry had 27,135 residents at the 2020 count, and the Bureau's July 2025 estimate stands at 29,217, which is 6.8 percent above its 2020 base. Across 2020 to 2024 the city shows 11,897 households, with 74.4 percent of homes lived in by their owners. The median home value is $266,500, the median rent is $1,553, and the median household earns $86,315.

With three of every four homes owner-occupied, most competing sellers are neighbors, and most buyers are either move-up families or investors eyeing a rehab. The mean trip to work takes 29.0 minutes.

sections.h2: How do McHenry's schools, roads and rail affect a sale?
sections.html:
Prospective buyers tend to open with schools and the commute. Two districts serve the city: McHenry Community High School District 156 and McHenry School District 15, which runs the elementary and middle schools.

  • Roads: Illinois Route 31 runs north and south and Route 120 runs east and west, and the two meet in the city center.
  • Rail: McHenry is the end of a branch of Metra's Union Pacific Northwest Line, with weekday service to Ogilvie Transportation Center in Chicago.
  • Trails and parks: the Prairie Trail crosses the middle of the city, and Moraine Hills State Park sits at the east end with Lake Defiance as its centerpiece.
  • Airports: O'Hare and Milwaukee Mitchell are the closest public international airports.

The city also has three downtown districts, along Green Street, Riverside Drive and Main Street, joined by a 0.73 mile Riverwalk. A house within walking distance of that stretch usually has a different buyer pool from a subdivision house on the edge of town.

sections.h2: Does McHenry's weather change how a house should be prepared?
sections.html:
Winter is the main factor. NOAA normals reported for McHenry show about 34.5 inches of snow a year, 22 days with measurable snow, and a January average daily low near 13 degrees. The all-time low on record is 32 below zero.

That history is why buyers look closely at roofs, gutters, attic insulation, furnaces and basements in this part of the state. Annual precipitation averages close to 37 inches, with May and June the wettest months, so a damp basement or sump pump that has been running hard is something an inspector will find.

The Fox River, Boone Creek and the glacial lakes around town make water a real feature of the area. If your lot is near the river or a creek, confirm its flood zone status with the city before you set a price.

sections.h2: Which city permits matter before you sell a McHenry house?
sections.html:
The City of McHenry requires building permits for most remodeling and home improvement work, so open permits and unpermitted projects are worth sorting out before a buyer's inspector asks. Call the Community Development Department at 815-363-2170 or visit the Municipal Center at 333 S Green Street.

The city says most residential permit applications are processed within 10 business days, and the clock does not start until everything needed for review has been submitted. Some permits are issued faster:

  • Reroof, siding, and windows or doors.
  • Water heater and furnace or air conditioner replacement.
  • Sewer or water repair.

These counter-based permits are issued at the time of application when you apply in person and within 24 hours when you apply online. Inspections are included in the permit fee, need 24 hours' notice, and are booked in three-hour windows. Roofing and siding inspections run from 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m.

When a previous owner skipped a permit, ask the department what it would take to close the file. An investor may shrug that off, whereas a buyer with a mortgage and an inspector may not.

sections.h2: What happens at the McHenry County Recorder when the deed is filed?
sections.html:
Recording happens at the county, not at city hall. The Recorder's Office reports that a conforming document paired with the correct fee gets recorded the day it arrives, and it aims to mail items back in roughly two working days. The fee schedule is available at 815-334-4110.

The office also explains that the PTAX-203 or MyDec form, which lists the full consideration, may travel with the deed. State transfer tax is fixed by 35 ILCS 200/31-15 at fifty cents for every $500 of value, and it is evidenced by revenue stamps.

One local detail: the Recorder's FAQ says no municipality in McHenry County adds a separate transfer tax, which differs from some suburbs elsewhere in Illinois. Parcel questions go to the Assessor at 815-334-4290, and tax bill questions go to the County Treasurer at 815-334-4072.

sections.h2: What must a McHenry seller disclose, and what happens to the water account?
sections.html:
The disclosure statute, 765 ILCS 77/20, places the burden on the seller: every item of the report completed, and the report delivered ahead of the signed contract. Finish it while you are still weighing offers.

City water and sewer bills arrive every two months, and accounts fall on even or odd billing months depending on the account number prefix. McHenry publishes a Water/Sewer Transfer Form that records the ownership date along with billing addresses for the outgoing and incoming owner. Submitting it gives you a firm cutoff date for the final bill.

Line up what the title company will want as well: a mortgage payoff letter if one exists, the parcel number, a recent tax bill and any open permit paperwork.

sections.h2: How do the three ways to sell a McHenry house compare?
sections.html:
Set the three paths side by side before choosing.

  • Agent listing: the largest audience, in return for showings, an appraisal and inspection, and possible repair requests from the buyer.
  • Owner-handled sale: control over price and timing, with the paperwork and promotion landing on you.
  • Direct sale for cash: quicker and with fewer conditions, at a price that accounts for the work the house needs.

With any offer, insist on a written copy and read each closing cost line.

faqs.q: Is a permit needed for a new roof or water heater in McHenry?
faqs.a: Yes. Reroofing and water heater replacement both appear on the city's list of counter-based permits, issued on the spot for in-person applications and within a day for online ones. Community Development, at 815-363-2170, can confirm what your project needs.

faqs.q: Does the City of McHenry add a transfer stamp of its own?
faqs.a: It does not. The county Recorder's FAQ says no municipality in the county levies a separate transfer tax, which leaves the state charge of fifty cents for every $500 under 35 ILCS 200/31-15.

faqs.q: Which office records the deed on a McHenry sale?
faqs.a: The McHenry County Recorder, reachable at 815-334-4110. The office records conforming documents with the right fee the same day and aims to return them in about two working days.

faqs.q: What happens to the city water account at a McHenry closing?
faqs.a: McHenry bills water and sewer every second month and offers a Water/Sewer Transfer Form that records the ownership date. File it at closing so the last bill and the new owner's first bill start on the right dates.

faqs.q: Can a McHenry house with deferred repairs still be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The state asks for a completed disclosure report ahead of the contract, and whatever repairs follow are negotiated with the buyer. A buyer using a mortgage will often press for fixes, whereas an investor may price them in and skip the repair requests.
